### Observed differences

- In the earlier window the activities A26–A30 typically ran before A25 (A26 before A25 in about 97 in 100 traces; A28, A29, A30 before A25 in 80–85 in 100), and A26 typically ran before the trio A20/A21/A22 (about 77 in 100), while pairs between A20–A22 and A28–A30 appeared in both orders (e.g. A20 before A28 in 57.5 in 100, A21 before A30 in 50.5 in 100). In the later window this is inverted and fixed: A20–A22 and A25 precede A26–A30 in 97–100 in 100 traces (A25 before A26 in about 99.5 in 100), and no pair shows both orders any more. Both activities of every pair still occur together in 200 of 200 traces in both windows, so participation itself did not change. [REL001, REL002, REL008, REL018, REL020, REL021, REL022]
- Reverse-order adjacencies disappeared: A26 followed by A24 within five steps occurs in 108 of 200 traces before versus 1 after; A28 followed by A20 in 70 versus 1; A29 followed by A20 in 93 versus 1; A30 followed by A20 in 82 versus 1. [LAG031, LAG037, LAG043, LAG049]
- Successor choice concentrated into a fixed chain. A25's observed outgoing transitions went from A36 about 45 in 100, A27 18, A30 13, A28 10 and A26 2, to A26 about 99.5 in 100; A27 now leads to A36 in about 84 in 100 (before 45); A35, previously split between A26 (53) and A24 (46), now leads only to A24; A20, A21 and A22, previously followed by most of the block, now lead almost only to one another and to A25 (about 30–36 in 100 each); A26 no longer shows A24 (about 17 in 100 before) or the A20–A22 trio as successors and now leads to A29, A28 and A30 (42/33/26). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR010]
- Execution within the block became consecutive: A20, A21 and A22 follow one another at 1–2 steps in nearly every trace (A21 then A22 at 1–2 steps in about 60 in 100 before, 100 in 100 after); A25 follows the trio at 1–3 steps; A24 precedes A25 at exactly 4 steps in 200 of 200 traces (before, at 4–5 steps in only 50 of 200); A27 follows A25 at exactly 5 steps in 200 of 200 traces; A36 follows A27 immediately in about 84 in 100 traces (before 48). [LAG001, LAG009, LAG010, LAG025, LAG027, LAG036]
- Relative positions shifted consistently: A20–A22, A24 and A25 occur earlier in the trace (mean relative position of A25 0.70 → 0.60, of A20 0.61 → 0.55), while A26–A30 occur later (A26 0.53 → 0.63; A29 and A30 0.61 → 0.68). [POS001, POS003, POS005, POS006, POS009, POS010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the execution order of the block A20–A30 was re-sequenced. In the earlier window A25 ran after the group A26–A30 and A26 ran before the trio A20/A21/A22, with many pairs in both orders; in the later window the same activities form a fixed sequence in which A35 is immediately followed by A24, then the trio A20/A21/A22 in varying order, then A25, A26, the trio A28/A29/A30, and A27 followed by A36, with routing into these successors near-deterministic (A25 → A26 in about 99.5 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions, A27 → A36 in about 84 in 100, A35 → A24 exclusively). [REL018, REL020, DIR004, DIR006, DIR010, LAG027]

The hypothesis rests on direct relational and positional evidence rather than on participation: all 22 relation items shift in the same direction while each pair still co-occurs in 200 of 200 traces in both windows; reverse-order adjacencies fall from roughly 40–110 of 200 traces to about 1; and the relative positions of A25 and A26 cross (0.70 → 0.60 versus 0.53 → 0.63). The volume of qualifying items (100 against roughly 1 expected by chance among 189 tested units) cannot be explained by sampling variation, and every item's difference exceeds about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled data. [LAG031, LAG049, POS005, POS006]

An important competing explanation remains: a shift in the relative share of pre-existing execution variants that differ in order would produce similar window-level relation and direction profiles, and the window-level aggregates cannot separate this from a within-trace re-sequencing. Direction shares also cover only observed outgoing transitions, so successors that are no longer observed (for example A25 → A36) may still occur occasionally; position and lag statements concern event positions, not clock time. [DIR004]

Other differences: a handful of rare transitions (about 1 in 200 each) appear or vanish at the margin — in the later window A20 shows isolated new successors such as A09, A11, A18, A35 and A42, while rare successors such as A48 after A21 or A30 are no longer observed; these sit at the edge of observability. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR009]
